lines: AI agents can now pay on their own. Sentinel makes sure they never pay a scammer.
This is Sentinel L-one, our Avalanche chain.
First, without Sentinel. We switch the guard off, and ask a shopping agent for an Apple Watch Ultra 2, at the best price.
It compares the shops and picks Meridian, the cheapest. A ghost store, nine days old. The agent fills in the card, and pays.
Now the same request, with the guard on. The agent doesn't even know Sentinel exists. It clicks pay, as before.
Instead, the payment goes to our MCP server first. Eight layers check it.
Meridian claims a French company number. Sentinel checks it live with the state registry, data dot gouv. It doesn't exist. Trust: seventeen. Refused.
The refusal is written on Sentinel L-one, with its proof. Here it is, in our explorer.
And here it is live, on city dot petroi dot F R. The payment becomes a car. It is scanned at the gate, turned away, and sent to the scrapyard. Its address joins the threat registry.
An unusual amount at a known shop is not a scam, but it isn't normal either. Sentinel holds it, and a human decides. One click approves it, and the visa is issued.
In the city, the parked car leaves, green.
An ordinary payment goes straight through. Trust: one hundred. A one-time visa, written on chain.
The car drives into the C-Chain, where the money actually lands.
And the scammer tries again. This time there is nothing to compute: the address is already on the registry. Refused instantly, for every agent.
Every visa and every decision is a transaction on Sentinel L-one, paid in S-E-C.
Sentinel. Your AI agents never lose your money.
